meta_description: The Brunei Half Marathon 2026 review: November 21 at the Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge -- Southeast Asia's longest bridge, opened 2020.
dek: Set for 21 November 2026 at the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien Bridge, this race starts near Southeast Asia's longest bridge -- a 30-kilometre span connecting Brunei's mainland to its Temburong exclave, opened in 2020.
verdict: The Brunei Half Marathon starts near a genuinely remarkable piece of infrastructure: the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien Bridge, a 30-kilometre dual-carriageway span across Brunei Bay -- the longest bridge in Southeast Asia, completed in 2019 at a cost of B$1.6 billion and opened in March 2020. That's a genuine engineering landmark to anchor a race around, distinct from anything else covered in this research batch. Three distances (5K/10K/21K) with open registration make this a straightforward pick for runners interested in Brunei -- a country rarely covered by races in this dataset.

sections.heading: Racing Near Southeast Asia's Longest Bridge
paragraphs: The race is held at the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien (SHOAS) Bridge in Bandar Seri Begawan, offering 5K, 10K and 21K distances. [1] The bridge itself spans Brunei Bay, connecting the Bruneian mainland to its semi-exclave of Temburong District -- at 30 kilometres, it's the longest bridge in all of Southeast Asia. [2]

sections.heading: A Recent Engineering Achievement
paragraphs: Construction began in mid-2014 and finished in 2019 at a cost of B$1.6 billion, with the bridge officially opening on 17 March 2020. [2] It's the first road bridge to directly link Brunei's mainland with the Temburong exclave, letting commuters skip the four immigration checkpoints previously required via the route through Malaysia. The bridge's design incorporates star and crescent symbols at its highest points, reflecting Brunei's identity as a Muslim state.
